edit.description: the named-note arm takes its verdict from the channel's one listing instead of re-deriving a note predicate beside it
the refusal over a directory child, beside the dot-prefixed and absent-name arms

summary: `flume friction <name>` re-derives what counts as a note beside the channel's one listing, so a directory child exits 74 where the shipped help page promises 2

per.section: The fix lands at the mechanism

acceptance: a name the channel's own listing holds no note for refuses as absent, whatever stands at the path, so the only `EX_IOERR` the named arm can take is a read that actually failed — the disposition the shipped help page states
tests: flume friction refuses a name the channel's listing holds no note for as absent rather than unreadable
notes: Measured this tick over a channel holding a subdirectory: `flume friction subdir` exits 74, `EISDIR`. `isNote` (`src/cli.ts:801`) is `isDirectChild && !isDotName`; `frictionNotes` (`src/friction.ts:117`) is `isFile() && !isDotName`, so the bare list omits what the named arm refuses to classify. The shipped page promises exit 2 for a name naming no file (`src/cliHelp.ts:422`) and scopes 74 to the channel dir or a note in it (`:429`).
